- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive; apply a “cool-down” correction to dampen the peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has moved >5% from 18-day average, model often fails to revert; apply a “reversion bias” correction toward historical mean in 3-5 day horizon.
- Forecasts for 30-day horizon show persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1-2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a “sentiment reversal” correction with 2-3 day lag to align with sentiment shift.
